name: Docs / Changelog / Status
description: A clean documentation / release-notes / status page: a sticky sidebar table of contents, an intro, content sections (each with a heading, body text, and an optional code block), and a versioned changelog. A status badge in the header signals health. Use for 'write a docs page / API reference / changelog / release notes / status page for X'.

product.description: Product / project name in the header.

theme.description: Color scheme: 'dark' (default) or 'light'. Code blocks stay dark in both.

accent.description: Hex accent color for links, the active nav item, and the status dot.

status_label.description: Short status text in the header badge (e.g. 'All systems operational', 'v2.1.0'). Optional.

status_ok.description: Set to any truthy value for a green/healthy badge; set to null/empty for a neutral (amber) badge.

nav.description: Sidebar table-of-contents links. Hrefs should match the section ids you use (e.g. '#install'). Mark one item active with active:true.

intro.description: Intro paragraph under the main heading.
intro.default: Everything you need to install, configure, and ship with Aurora. Start with the overview, then jump to the section you need from the sidebar.

quicklinks.description: Optional card grid right under the intro — a docs-home jump list (3 read best). Each has a label, a one-line body, and a link (usually a section anchor). Set to null to hide.

default.label: Install
default.body: Get up and running in under a minute.

default.label: Quickstart
default.body: Your first query in three lines.

default.label: Configuration
default.body: Override any default when you need to.

sections.description: Documentation sections in order. Each has an id (sidebar anchor target), a heading, body text (plain paragraphs; double newlines for paragraph breaks), an OPTIONAL code block with an OPTIONAL lang label shown in the code window, and an OPTIONAL note callout (supports inline HTML like 'Tip:').

default.heading: Overview
default.body: Aurora is a small, fast toolkit for building data products. It has no required configuration and works out of the box, but every default can be overridden when you need to.
default.note: New here? Start with Install, then follow the Quickstart end to end.

default.heading: Install
default.body: Install from your package manager of choice. Aurora ships as a single dependency with no native build step.
default.code:
npm install aurora
# or
pnpm add aurora

default.heading: Quickstart
default.body: Import the client, point it at your data source, and run your first query in three lines.

default.heading: Configuration
default.body: Configuration is optional. Pass an options object to the constructor, or set environment variables — explicit options always win over the environment.
default.note: Tip: Keep secrets in the environment, not in source.

changelog.description: Release entries, newest first. Each has a version, a date, and a list of change lines (each {text: ...}, optionally tagged 'Added'/'Fixed'/'Changed' via tag).

New client API — see the migration guide.
